whisper.label: Whisper Large-V3
whisper.text:
Hi, this is Nusheen Rostami. I'm an artist based in New York. It's very exciting to have an opening in 2020. It feels like a surreal dream.
I was happy to be able to kind of connect to a community of artists who also work with different approaches of the same material.
The piece here is called Zaman. Zaman in Farsi means time. The same as when you refer to time as an era or time as in the way that we perceive time.
The basic concepts of Zaman are the same as the concepts of the world.
The basic concept of it is that from a similar shape, which is the shape of a circle, that these rotating circles are surfaces of different materials and they're all activated with a spotlight.
Spotlight being this light that is actually LED spotlight. It's very dim and concentrated.
But because of that concentrated rays of light, it projects, I call it, drawing of light.
So I wanted sort of a narrative of all these circles.
These circles that are rotating under spotlights and each of them, based on the material that they have, reflect a different drawing.
And together they sort of create a narrative of this extraterrestrial landscape in the horizons.
And I call it a landscape because it's sort of, it's an invitation to look afar into a distance and to imagine.
And I find light to be that material that sort of, you know, you close your eyes, you can still see the light.
You open your eyes, you see your eyes immediately are capturing light.
It is the same kind of like process that we do when we want to dream, when we want to imagine.
We still like in our dreams.
That idea of a light is forming images for us.
So this landscape that invites you to look afar is sort of, it's an invitation to imagine.
And I find it to be a time that we need to all dream again and to imagine.
Because of the kind of fear that we've all been struggling with as human.
In the darkest of the time, there is more need for light.
For me, it's kind of like a hopeful work that invites the audience to also dream and have a positive outlook, hopefully.
And I think that's what I'm trying to do.
Thank you.
